newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican authorities arrest 14 alleged rebels.
newsitem.headline: Mexican authorities arrest 14 alleged rebels.

text.p: Mexican police and army units have arrested 14 alleged leftist guerrillas in the southern state of Oaxaca, officials said on Thursday.

The 14 people are accused of belonging to the Popular Revolutionary Army (EPR) and of taking part in the rebel group's biggest attacks to date, on Aug. 28 this year, Oaxaca state government officials said.
The hardline leftist EPR appeared for the first time in June this year and two months later carried out attacks on army and police targets in several states in which at least 15 people died.
Oaxaca state prosecutor Roberto Martinez told a news conference the arrests were made in the Pacific coast Loxicha area of the state, one of Mexico's poorest.

The Mexican Human Rights Defence League said six people had been arrested and 17 had disappeared during the counterinsurgency sweeps, which involved more than 400 policemen and soldiers. It was not immediately clear if any of those alleged to be missing were among the 14 arrested.

Martinez said that among those held was the interim mayor of San Agustin Loxicha, Gaudencio Matias. Matias had taken over from mayor Agustin Luna, who was arrested along with 16 others on Sept. 25 on similar charges of belonging to the EPR.
